sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: This week, the Supreme Court heard a case that, on its surface, appears to be a routine dispute over a government fee.
sentences.zh: 本周，最高法院审理了一起案件，表面上看，这似乎只是关于政府收费的常规纠纷。

sentences.en: In reality, it could transform how every industry in the country is regulated.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，它可能会改变全国各行业的监管方式。

sentences.en: My colleague, Adam Liptak, explains.
sentences.zh: 我的同事亚当·利普塔克将为您解读。

sentences.en: It's Friday, January 19th.
sentences.zh: 今天是1月19日，星期五。

sentences.en: Adam, welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 亚当，欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Hello, Michael.
sentences.zh: 你好，迈克尔。

sentences.en: So, Adam, remind us of the essential facts of this case that just ended up before the Supreme Court a few days ago, a case that I know you see as among the most important
sentences.zh: 那么，亚当，请提醒我们这起几天前刚提交到最高法院的案件的基本事实，我知道你认为这是本届最高法院最重要的案件之一，

sentences.en: and consequential of this Supreme Court term.
sentences.zh: 也是影响最深远的案件之一。

sentences.en: What, on paper, is it about?
sentences.zh: 从书面上看，它到底是关于什么的？

sentences.en: So, this case is about herring fishermen in Cape May, New Jersey.
sentences.zh: 这起案件是关于新泽西州开普梅的鲱鱼渔民的。

sentences.en: I went to visit them, and among the people I talked to was a fisherman named Bill Bright.
sentences.zh: 我去拜访了他们，在交谈过的人中，有一位名叫比尔·布莱特的渔民。

sentences.en: First-generation fisherman.
sentences.zh: 第一代渔民。

sentences.en: I've been fishing for 40 years.
sentences.zh: 我捕鱼已经40年了。

sentences.en: I actually quit my union job to try fishing, and I've been fishing ever since.
sentences.zh: 我其实是辞掉了工会的工作才尝试捕鱼的，从那以后我就一直干这一行。

sentences.en: Can you ask how old you are?
sentences.zh: 能问问你多大年纪了吗？
我64岁了。

sentences.en: I'm 63, so you're a pulver.
sentences.zh: 我63岁，所以你是个老手。

sentences.en: And I'm probably not wiser.
sentences.zh: 而且我可能并不比你更聪明。

sentences.en: And they told me that they have long been living under a 1976 law that requires them to take federal observers out with them on their fishing trips.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉我，他们长期以来一直生活在1976年的一项法律之下，该法律要求他们带联邦观察员一起出海捕鱼。

sentences.en: They go out for a week at a time.
sentences.zh: 他们每次出海一周。

sentences.en: And those observers gather data to prevent overfishing.
sentences.zh: 这些观察员负责收集数据以防止过度捕捞。

sentences.en: What has the role of government been over the years?
sentences.zh: 多年来，政府的角色是什么？

sentences.en: The role of the government has slowly been increasing,
sentences.zh: 政府的角色一直在缓慢增加，

sentences.en: which has been warranted in a lot of situations, because we do need quotas for every fishery.
sentences.zh: 在很多情况下这是合理的，因为我们确实需要为每个渔场设定配额。

sentences.en: We know that.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道这一点。

sentences.en: And what they told me was that they like the observers.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉我，他们并不反感观察员。

sentences.en: They think the observers are valuable.
sentences.zh: 他们认为观察员很有价值。

sentences.en: They're on board, so to speak, with the observers.
sentences.zh: 可以说，他们是支持观察员上船的。

sentences.en: So over-management and the role of the government has been a good thing overall, because we know without that, most of us would not be fishing to them.
sentences.zh: 所以，过度管理和政府的角色总体上是一件好事，因为我们知道没有这些，我们大多数人可能就没法捕鱼了。

sentences.en: But come 2020, the agency in charge of this program called the National Marine Fisheries Service takes a turn and says, not only do you have to take the observers out with you,
sentences.zh: 但到了2020年，负责该项目的机构——国家海洋渔业局——态度发生了转变，他们说，不仅你们必须带观察员出海，

sentences.en: but you have to pay for the privilege.
sentences.zh: 而且你们还必须为这项特权付费。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Partly because the agency was low on funds, partly because they wanted to expand the program.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是该机构资金不足，部分原因是他们想扩大该项目。

sentences.en: And the fishermen had a problem with that.
sentences.zh: 渔民们对此有意见。

sentences.en: They had a practical problem, they told me.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉我，他们面临着实际困难。

sentences.en: Give me a sense of the actual dollars and the cents.
sentences.zh: 能具体说说金额吗？

sentences.en: How much did they want you to pay for the monitors?
sentences.zh: 他们要求你们为监督员支付多少钱？

sentences.en: At what percentage?
sentences.zh: 按什么比例？

sentences.en: At the time, but this is pre-pandemic price, was $700 a day.
sentences.zh: 当时，这是疫情前的价格，是每天700美元。

sentences.en: Because that is a significant cut of their profits.
sentences.zh: 因为这对他们的利润来说是一笔巨大的削减。

sentences.en: That's the monitor would get $5,000.
sentences.zh: 也就是说监督员能拿到5000美元。

sentences.en: That's pretty close at 5% of a good trip that a crew member would get.
sentences.zh: 这差不多相当于船员在一次好收成中能分到的5%。

sentences.en: So he would get the same on a good trip that a crew member would get.
sentences.zh: 所以他在一次好收成中拿到的钱和船员一样多。

sentences.en: But on a bad trip, he still gets a five grand and they get next to nothing.
sentences.zh: 但在收成不好的时候，他依然能拿五千，而他们几乎一无所获。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And they have a kind of philosophical legal problem with it, too.
sentences.zh: 而且他们在哲学和法律层面上也对此有异议。

sentences.en: They say the 1976 law doesn't authorize these payments and that the agency shouldn't be allowed to interpret the law to say that it does.
sentences.zh: 他们说1976年的法律并未授权这些费用，机构不应被允许通过解读法律来声称其有权收费。

sentences.en: So what's your reaction to the idea that you should not only host the monitor but pay for the monitor?
sentences.zh: 那么，对于不仅要接待监督员还要为其付费的想法，你有什么反应？

sentences.en: I don't think it's fair.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这不公平。

sentences.en: And I also now, with everything that we have going with the rising costs, especially after the pandemic, to tack that onto us,
sentences.zh: 而且现在，考虑到我们面临的所有不断上涨的成本，特别是在疫情之后，还要把这笔费用强加给我们，

sentences.en: that tax is going to be very burdensome to a business that's very burdened in the beginning.
sentences.zh: 这笔税费对于一个本来就负担沉重的企业来说将是非常沉重的。

sentences.en: So, Adam, this feels like a pretty small-scale dispute over basically who should pay for the implementation of this government regulation, that there be monitors on these boats.
sentences.zh: 所以，亚当，这感觉像是一场规模很小的纠纷，本质上是关于谁应该为政府法规的实施买单，即在这些船上配备监督员。

sentences.en: Yeah, it barely feels like a Supreme Court case, right?
sentences.zh: 是啊，这几乎不像是一个最高法院案件，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's a routine legal dispute, but it has embedded in it a huge question.
sentences.zh: 这是一场常规的法律纠纷，但其中蕴含着一个巨大的问题。

sentences.en: And that's the question of who gets to decide what this 1976 federal law means or what any federal law means.
sentences.zh: 那就是：谁有权决定1976年的这项联邦法律意味着什么，或者任何联邦法律意味着什么？

sentences.en: Is it the agency in charge of implementing it?
sentences.zh: 是负责实施该法律的机构吗？

sentences.en: Or should it be a judge without giving any particular kind of deference to the agency?
sentences.zh: 还是应该由法官来决定，而不给予该机构任何特殊的尊重？

sentences.en: And that takes us to a 1984 landmark Supreme Court case, one of the most cited, most influential cases in our history, called Chevron v.
sentences.zh: 这把我们带到了1984年最高法院的一个里程碑式案件，这是我们历史上被引用最多、最有影响力的案件之一，名为雪佛龙诉

sentences.en: Natural Defense Resources Council.
sentences.zh: 自然资源保护委员会案。

sentences.en: That case gave rise to a concept called Chevron deference, which is not about deferring to Chevron, the oil company,
sentences.zh: 该案引出了一个概念，叫“雪佛龙尊重原则”，这并不是指尊重雪佛龙石油公司，

sentences.en: but about the precedent set out in that case about who should get deference.
sentences.zh: 而是指该案确立的关于谁应该获得尊重的先例。

sentences.en: Chevron deference says that if a statute passed by Congress is ambiguous,
sentences.zh: 雪佛龙尊重原则规定，如果国会通过的法规含糊不清，

sentences.en: the agency gets to interpret what it means, so long as its interpretation is reasonable.
sentences.zh: 只要机构的解释是合理的，该机构就有权解释其含义。

sentences.en: And courts have to defer to the agency's interpretation, that is, judges who are ordinarily in charge of saying what the law means
sentences.zh: 法院必须尊重机构的解释，也就是说，通常负责解释法律含义的法官，

sentences.en: and what statutes mean have to put the thumb on the scale in favor of federal agencies, expert agencies, on what congressionally enacted statutes mean.
sentences.zh: 以及解释法规含义的法官，在面对国会制定的法规时，必须在天平上加码，偏向联邦机构，即专家机构。

sentences.en: So under the Chevron deference doctrine, these fishermen don't really seem to have much of a legal case here, right?
sentences.zh: 那么在雪佛龙尊重原则下，这些渔民在这里似乎并没有太多的法律依据，对吧？

sentences.en: The doctrine says that if that 1976 law is in any way unclear on the question of who pays for these monitors, a government agency is going to make that call
sentences.zh: 该原则规定，如果1976年的法律在谁支付监督员费用这一问题上有任何不明确之处，政府机构将做出决定，

sentences.en: and a government agency has made the call that the fishermen pay.
sentences.zh: 而政府机构已经决定由渔民付费。

sentences.en: So that's more or less that.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上就是这样。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And when they sue, a federal appeals court says, the statute's ambiguous.
sentences.zh: 当他们起诉时，联邦上诉法院说，法规含糊不清。

sentences.en: That means the agency gets to decide.
sentences.zh: 这意味着机构有权决定。

sentences.en: The agency has decided.
sentences.zh: 机构已经做出了决定。

sentences.en: We, judges, are not going to do our own work in figuring out what the correct legal answer is.
sentences.zh: 我们法官不会自己去费力找出正确的法律答案是什么。

sentences.en: We're going to defer to the agency.
sentences.zh: 我们将尊重机构的决定。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And as you say, Michael, this case in itself is not super important.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，迈克尔，这起案件本身并不重要。

sentences.en: But this concept is woven through American law and has done work for decades to resolve cases on things like protecting the environment,
sentences.zh: 但这个概念贯穿于美国法律之中，几十年来一直在解决诸如环境保护、

sentences.en: workplace safety, consumer protection, nuclear power, almost everything you could imagine from all of the many federal agencies.
sentences.zh: 工作场所安全、消费者保护、核能等问题，几乎涵盖了你能想象到的所有联邦机构的事务。

sentences.en: The entire legal system is rooted in this idea that in cases where a statute is ambiguous, agencies rather than courts are going to be kind of at the front line
sentences.zh: 整个法律体系都植根于这样一个理念：在法规含糊不清的情况下，机构而不是法院将处于第一线，

sentences.en: in deciding what the law means.
sentences.zh: 来决定法律的含义。

sentences.en: Because, the thinking goes, they're the experts.
sentences.zh: 因为人们认为，他们是专家。

sentences.en: They know their subject matter areas.
sentences.zh: 他们了解自己的专业领域。

sentences.en: And they should have a role in the process of deciding what Congress meant to do.
sentences.zh: 他们应该在决定国会意图的过程中发挥作用。

sentences.en: Congress, of course, can't anticipate every development.
sentences.zh: 当然，国会无法预见每一个发展。

sentences.en: And the thinking behind Chevron is that it has at least implicitly delegated to agencies the opportunity to fill in the gaps and make statutes work on the ground.
sentences.zh: 雪佛龙背后的逻辑是，它至少隐性地授权机构去填补空白，让法规在实际中发挥作用。

sentences.en: It's very clear to me, Adam, how this doctrine benefits the executive branch and the dozens of agencies within it and all their experts because it forces judges to defer to them.
sentences.zh: 亚当，我很清楚这一原则如何使行政部门、其中的数十个机构及其所有专家受益，因为它迫使法官尊重他们。

sentences.en: However, if I'm in an industry being regulated by these agencies and these government workers, like these fishermen, I clearly view this differently.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果我身处一个受到这些机构和政府工作人员监管的行业，就像这些渔民一样，我显然会有不同的看法。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Business groups especially are very hostile to Chevron, hostile to what they call the administrative state, the power of executive agencies generally.
sentences.zh: 商业团体尤其敌视雪佛龙原则，敌视他们所说的“行政国家”，即行政机构的普遍权力。

sentences.en: And they have been looking for some time now to find the perfect vehicle to take down the Chevron doctrine, to do away with it.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在寻找完美的载体来推翻雪佛龙原则，废除它。

sentences.en: For practical reasons, they don't like being regulated.
sentences.zh: 出于实际原因，他们不喜欢被监管。

sentences.en: For philosophical reasons, they think judges should take the leading role in saying what the law is.
sentences.zh: 出于哲学原因，他们认为法官应该在解释法律方面发挥主导作用。

sentences.en: And these fishermen in New Jersey, along with another group in Rhode Island, are represented by well-funded conservative groups
sentences.zh: 新泽西州的这些渔民，连同罗德岛的另一个团体，由资金雄厚的保守派团体代理，

sentences.en: with financial ties to Charles Koch, the conservative billionaire.
sentences.zh: 这些团体与保守派亿万富翁查尔斯·科赫有财务联系。

sentences.en: And this case seems to be a very likely vehicle to undo the key precedent in this area of the law.
sentences.zh: 这起案件似乎极有可能成为推翻该法律领域关键先例的载体。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So we should not be viewing this case as simply the story of local fishermen who don't want to pay for the monitors on their boats who are counting up how many fish they catch.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不应该仅仅把这起案件看作是当地渔民不想为船上的监督员付费的故事，他们只是在数数自己捕了多少鱼。

sentences.en: We should view it in the much broader landscape of an ongoing conservative effort to dismantle regulation and prevent the government
sentences.zh: 我们应该将其置于更广阔的背景下看待，这是一场持续的保守派努力，旨在拆解监管并阻止政府

sentences.en: from playing the role that it does in regulating the companies like the ones that Charles Koch runs.
sentences.zh: 在监管查尔斯·科赫所经营的那类公司时发挥其应有的作用。

sentences.en: Yeah, this case is both small and easy to understand
sentences.zh: 是的，这起案件既小又容易理解，

sentences.en: because if the fishermen win, it will be on the ground that chevron deference goes out the window.
sentences.zh: 因为如果渔民赢了，理由将是雪佛龙尊重原则被废除。

sentences.en: And all of American law, based on the activities of countless federal agencies,
sentences.zh: 而所有基于无数联邦机构活动的美国法律，

sentences.en: becomes reshaped.
sentences.zh: 都将被重塑。

sentences.en: And power is shifted from agencies to an extent to Congress, to a probably larger extent to the courts,
sentences.zh: 权力将从机构转移到国会，在更大程度上转移到法院，

sentences.en: and regulation becomes harder to implement.
sentences.zh: 监管将变得更难实施。

sentences.en: Across the board.
sentences.zh: 全面如此。

sentences.en: In every imaginable federal setting, yeah.
sentences.zh: 在所有能想象到的联邦领域，是的。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我编写《纽约时报》游戏中的拼图游戏《Connections》，我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫“联觉”的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由人制作的，就像你们刚才听到的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 前往nytimes.com/games立即开始游戏。

sentences.en: So Adam, how do these oral arguments in the case unfold?
sentences.zh: 那么亚当，这起案件的口头辩论是如何展开的？

sentences.en: So Wednesday morning.
sentences.zh: 周三上午。

sentences.en: You'll hear argument first this morning in case 22-12-19.
sentences.zh: 今天上午你们将首先听到22-12-19号案件的辩论。

sentences.en: The court hears arguments, starting with Roman Martinez, a lawyer for the Fisherman.
sentences.zh: 法院听取了辩论，首先是渔民的律师罗曼·马丁内斯。

sentences.en: Mr. Chief Justice, and may I please the court, for too long, Chevron has distorted the judicial process and undermined statutory interpretation.
sentences.zh: 首席大法官，请允许我向法庭陈述，长期以来，雪佛龙原则扭曲了司法程序，破坏了法定解释。

sentences.en: Who makes a couple of basic points.
sentences.zh: 他提出了几个基本观点。

sentences.en: Article 3 empowers judges to say what the law is.
sentences.zh: 宪法第三条授权法官解释法律。

sentences.en: It requires them to interpret federal statutes using their best and independent judgment.
sentences.zh: 它要求他们用自己最好且独立的判断来解释联邦法规。

sentences.en: Chevron undermines that duty.
sentences.zh: 雪佛龙原则破坏了这一职责。

sentences.en: That the separation of powers gives the judiciary, in Article 3 of the Constitution, the obligation to say what the law is, and that Chevron was wrong from the start.
sentences.zh: 宪法第三条规定的权力分立赋予了司法机构解释法律的义务，而雪佛龙原则从一开始就是错误的。

sentences.en: There's no reason to think that Congress intends every ambiguity and every agency statute
sentences.zh: 没有理由认为国会打算让每一个模糊之处和每一个机构法规

sentences.en: to give agencies an ongoing power to interpret and reinterpret federal law in ways that override its best meaning.
sentences.zh: 都赋予机构持续的权力，以凌驾于法律最佳含义之上的方式来解释和重新解释联邦法律。

sentences.en: And can be overruled, notwithstanding the usual rule that the Supreme Court should not discard precedents unless they were egregiously wrong and have proved unworkable.
sentences.zh: 而且可以被推翻，尽管最高法院通常不应推翻先例，除非它们错得离谱且已被证明不可行。

sentences.en: If we have the best view of the statute, we should win this case.
sentences.zh: 如果我们对法规有最好的解读，我们就应该赢得这场官司。

sentences.en: I welcome the court's questions.
sentences.zh: 我欢迎法庭的提问。

sentences.en: So Martinez's argument is that the Chevron deference doctrine is egregiously wrong and should be discarded, and that under it, far too much power to interpret regulations
sentences.zh: 马丁内斯的论点是，雪佛龙尊重原则错得离谱，应该被废除，而且根据该原则，解释法规的权力被赋予了政府机构，而不是法官，这实在太多了。

sentences.en: is being automatically given to government agencies rather than judges.
sentences.zh: 这种权力被自动赋予了政府机构，而不是法官。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, let me give you a few more examples along the same lines, Mr. Martinez.
sentences.zh: 好吧，马丁内斯先生，让我再给你举几个类似的例子。

sentences.en: And that almost immediately gets pushed back from the liberal justices who do everything they can to try to save the doctrine.
sentences.zh: 自由派大法官们几乎立刻进行了反击，他们竭尽全力试图挽救这一原则。

sentences.en: And one of the things they do, which is what judges do, is throw out hypothetical questions, testing what the world would look like if we didn't have Chevron.
sentences.zh: 他们所做的事情之一，也是法官们常做的事，就是抛出假设性问题，测试如果我们没有雪佛龙原则，世界会是什么样子。

sentences.en: So I was thinking, what is the next big piece of legislation on the horizon?
sentences.zh: 所以我当时在想，即将到来的下一项重大立法是什么？

sentences.en: And who knows?
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: Don't have a crystal ball.
sentences.zh: 我没有水晶球。

sentences.en: But I'm going to say, I'm going to guess that it's artificial intelligence.
sentences.zh: 但我会说，我猜是人工智能。

sentences.en: Justice Elena Kagan imagines, not a huge feat of imagination, that Congress may sometime pass a law addressing artificial intelligence.
sentences.zh: 埃琳娜·卡根大法官想象——这并不需要太大的想象力——国会可能在某个时候通过一项针对人工智能的法律。

sentences.en: Congress knows that there are going to be gaps because Congress can hardly see a week in the future with respect to this subject, let alone a year or a decade in the future.
sentences.zh: 国会知道会有漏洞，因为国会对于这个主题，连未来一周都难以预见，更不用说未来一年或十年了。

sentences.en: That law would, by nature, have to be general, have to contain ambiguities because it's such a fast-evolving part of modern life.
sentences.zh: 这项法律本质上必须是笼统的，必须包含模糊之处，因为这是现代生活中发展极其迅速的一部分。

sentences.en: Does the Congress want this court to decide those questions, policy-leading questions of artificial intelligence?
sentences.zh: 国会希望由法院来决定这些问题，即人工智能领域那些主导政策的问题吗？

sentences.en: And Congress would probably expect that, she says, an expert agency would interpret it, fill in the gaps, make it applicable, make it useful, and not some random judge somewhere
sentences.zh: 她说，国会可能会期望由专家机构来解释它，填补空白，使其适用，使其有用，而不是由某个地方的随机法官来决定，

sentences.en: in the country with no expertise at all.
sentences.zh: 那个法官在全国范围内根本没有任何专业知识。

sentences.en: And what she's really getting at, Adam, is that the virtue of the Chavon Doctrine is that
sentences.zh: 亚当，她真正想表达的是，雪佛龙原则的优点在于

sentences.en: it ensures that subject matter experts within these agencies are going to take the reins when
sentences.zh: 它确保了这些机构内部的主题专家将在

sentences.en: Congress inevitably writes that necessarily ambiguous rule.
sentences.zh: 国会不可避免地写下那些必然模糊的规则时掌握主导权。

sentences.en: And she's picking AI because it's a perfect test case of the most complicated area in the universe in which you'd want that subject matter expert to weigh in.
sentences.zh: 她选择人工智能是因为它是最复杂的领域，是你想让主题专家发表意见的完美测试案例。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And in truth, many statutes are necessarily ambiguous and can't anticipate the future, but that doesn't answer the question of who should decide under our constitutional system.
sentences.zh: 事实上，许多法规必然是模糊的，无法预见未来，但这并没有回答在我们的宪法体制下谁应该做决定的问题。

sentences.en: And what Roman Martinez says is, listen, you can take account of what the agency says, but it's the judge's job in the end to make the decision without, you would say,
sentences.zh: 罗曼·马丁内斯说的是，听着，你可以考虑机构的说法，但最终做出决定是法官的工作，而不是——你会说——

sentences.en: abdicating the judicial role to, I'm going to put words in his mouth, an unelected bureaucrat.
sentences.zh: 将司法角色让给——我替他说出来——一个未经选举的官僚。

sentences.en: My point is, it's really convenient for some members of Congress not to have to tackle the
sentences.zh: 我的观点是，对于国会的一些成员来说，不必去处理

sentences.en: hard questions and to rely on their friends in the executive branch to get them everything they want.
sentences.zh: 难题，而是依靠他们在行政部门的朋友来获得他们想要的一切，这真的很方便。

sentences.en: Another lawyer, Paul Clement, representing the Fisherman, made the point that Chevron also makes life too easy for Congress.
sentences.zh: 另一位代表渔民的律师保罗·克莱门特指出，雪佛龙原则也让国会的生活变得太轻松了。

sentences.en: Ambiguity is not ours, a delegation.
sentences.zh: 模糊性不是我们的，而是一种授权。

sentences.en: And more often, what ambiguity is, I don't have enough votes in Congress to make it clear.
sentences.zh: 更多时候，模糊性意味着我在国会没有足够的票数来把它说清楚。

sentences.en: So I'm going to leave it ambiguous and then we'll give it to my friends in the agency and they'll take it from here.
sentences.zh: 所以我打算让它保持模糊，然后把它交给我在机构里的朋友，他们会从这里接手。

sentences.en: That Congress is incentivized to pass ambiguous laws when it could pass more careful ones.
sentences.zh: 国会有动力去通过模糊的法律，而本可以制定更谨慎的法律。

sentences.en: And that Congress kind of likes that because it is easier and gets them in less political trouble if they say general things rather than specific things.
sentences.zh: 国会有点喜欢这样，因为这更容易，而且如果他们说笼统的话而不是具体的话，他们遇到的政治麻烦就更少。

sentences.en: And Congress should not kind of delegate to the executive branch the lawmaking function.
sentences.zh: 国会不应该把立法职能委托给行政部门。

sentences.en: It's an interesting argument and it puts a whole lot of confidence in members of the United
sentences.zh: 这是一个有趣的论点，它对美国国会成员寄予了极大的信心。

sentences.en: States Congress.
sentences.zh: 作为政治理论，这很有道理。

sentences.en: As a matter of political theory, it makes a lot of sense.
sentences.zh: 作为2024年的政治现实，很难想象这个国会能够制定出多少明智的法律，更不用说那些紧密解决我们时代重大问题的复杂法律了。

sentences.en: As a matter of political reality in 2024, it's pretty hard to imagine that this Congress is going to be able to enact many sensible laws at all, much less intricate ones closely
sentences.zh: 作为政治现实，很难想象这个国会能够制定出多少明智的法律，更不用说那些紧密

sentences.en: addressing the major problems of our time.
sentences.zh: 解决我们时代重大问题的复杂法律了。

sentences.en: General Prelogger.
sentences.zh: 总检察长。

sentences.en: Mr. Chief Justice, and may it please the court.
sentences.zh: 首席大法官，法庭请允许我发言。

sentences.en: And when the lawyer for the government, Solicitor General Elizabeth Prelogger, gets up defending
sentences.zh: 当政府律师、总检察长伊丽莎白·普雷洛格站起来为雪佛龙原则辩护时，

sentences.en: the Chevron doctrine, she says that undoing a system we've lived with for some 40 years would result in chaos.
sentences.zh: 她说，推翻一个我们已经生活了大约40年的体系会导致混乱。

sentences.en: Congress, agencies, states, regulated parties, and the American public have all relied on Chevron
sentences.zh: 国会、机构、各州、受监管方和美国公众都依赖雪佛龙原则

sentences.en: and the regulations upheld under it to make important decisions that could be upended by overruling that framework.
sentences.zh: 以及根据该原则维持的法规来做出重要决定，而推翻该框架可能会颠覆这些决定。

sentences.en: And the court should not lightly make that step when Chevron, she says, has served us well.
sentences.zh: 她说，当雪佛龙原则服务良好时，法院不应轻易采取这一步骤。

sentences.en: And Prelogger also points out that the court has heard cases like this before, at least in a related setting.
sentences.zh: 普雷洛格还指出，法院以前曾审理过类似的案件，至少是在相关背景下。

sentences.en: And it has declined to overrule precedents that would cause so much chaos.
sentences.zh: 它拒绝推翻那些会导致如此多混乱的先例。

sentences.en: The court observed that it would be the rare overruling that would introduce so much instability into so many areas of the law, all in one blow.
sentences.zh: 法院观察到，很少有推翻先例的做法会一下子给法律的这么多领域带来如此大的不稳定。

sentences.en: Overruling Chevron would be an even greater and unwarranted shock to the legal system.
sentences.zh: 推翻雪佛龙原则将是对法律体系更大且毫无根据的冲击。

sentences.en: I welcome the court's questions.
sentences.zh: 我欢迎法院的提问。

sentences.en: General, Section 7.
sentences.zh: 总检察长，第七节。

sentences.en: And what's the response from the justices that overturning this doctrine would basically create the legal equivalent of an earthquake that would kind of shatter the system?
sentences.zh: 大法官们对此的回应是，推翻这一原则基本上会产生相当于地震的法律后果，从而粉碎整个体系，对此有何回应？

sentences.en: Well, one interesting response came from Chief Justice John Roberts.
sentences.zh: 嗯，一个有趣的回应来自首席大法官约翰·罗伯茨。

sentences.en: Counsel, you began by saying Chevron is foundational.
sentences.zh: 律师，你开头说雪佛龙原则是基础性的。

sentences.en: We get a lot of statutory interpretations from agencies.
sentences.zh: 我们从机构那里得到了很多法定解释。

sentences.en: And I don't know whether it was 14 or 16 years, we haven't relied on Chevron over that time.
sentences.zh: 我不知道是14年还是16年了，我们在这段时间里没有依赖过雪佛龙原则。

sentences.en: I mean, have we overruled it in practice, even if we've...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，即使我们已经……我们在实践中推翻它了吗？

sentences.en: We sort of said, what's the big deal?
sentences.zh: 我们有点说，这有什么大不了的？

sentences.en: We haven't cited Chevron in years.
sentences.zh: 我们多年来没有引用过雪佛龙原则了。

sentences.en: It's sort of dead to us already.
sentences.zh: 它对我们来说已经名存实亡了。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And that's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And that's because the court, as we've often talked about, Michael, has shifted to the right.
sentences.zh: 这是因为法院，正如我们经常谈到的，迈克尔，已经向右转了。

sentences.en: And one of the projects of the conservative legal movement that placed recent conservative justices on the court has been hostility to the administrative state and to Chevron.
sentences.zh: 将最近的保守派大法官安置在法院的保守派法律运动的项目之一，就是对行政国家和雪佛龙原则的敌意。

sentences.en: So, in a sense, this is already happening at the Supreme Court level.
sentences.zh: 所以，在某种意义上，这已经在最高法院层面发生了。

sentences.en: And you can see this from some sharp questions from one of Donald Trump's appointees, Justice Brett Kavanaugh.
sentences.zh: 你可以从唐纳德·特朗普任命的大法官布雷特·卡瓦诺的一些尖锐问题中看出这一点。

sentences.en: But the reality of how this works is Chevron itself ushers in shocks to the system every four or eight years.
sentences.zh: 但其运作的现实是，雪佛龙原则本身每四到八年就会给体系带来冲击。

sentences.en: When a new administration comes in, whether it's communications law or securities law or competition law or environmental law, it goes from pillar to poSt.
sentences.zh: 当新政府上台时，无论是通信法、证券法、竞争法还是环境法，它都会从一个极端走向另一个极端。

sentences.en: He says the idea that Chevron is a force for stability is exactly backwards, that executive agencies change their positions as administrations change.
sentences.zh: 他说，认为雪佛龙原则是稳定力量的想法完全是倒退的，行政机构会随着政府的更迭而改变立场。

sentences.en: Every four or eight years, he says, you get a different answer to the question of what does the law mean?
sentences.zh: 他说，每四到八年，你对法律意味着什么这个问题就会得到不同的答案。

sentences.en: That is not stability.
sentences.zh: 那不是稳定。

sentences.en: And so I think to hold up stability and reliance is a little tough given just watching how it operates every four years.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，鉴于观察它每四年的运作方式，坚持稳定和依赖有点困难。

sentences.en: It feels like there could be some truth to that.
sentences.zh: 感觉这可能有一些道理。

sentences.en: What is the government lawyer's response to what Kavanaugh is claiming here?
sentences.zh: 政府律师对卡瓦诺在这里的主张有什么回应？

sentences.en: Prelaga responds that if there's authentic ambiguity in the law that Congress passed,
sentences.zh: 普雷洛格回应说，如果国会通过的法律中确实存在真正的模糊性，

sentences.en: then Congress would know that different presidential administrations might have different ways of thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 那么国会就会知道，不同的总统政府可能会有不同的思考方式。

sentences.en: And she says there's nothing inherently wrong with that.
sentences.zh: 她说这本身并没有什么错。

sentences.en: She says getting rid of Chevron, though, would create a whole new level of instability.
sentences.zh: 但她说，废除雪佛龙原则会造成一个全新的不稳定水平。

sentences.en: But there are 800 district court judges around the nation,
sentences.zh: 全国有800名地方法官，

sentences.en: and I think it's fair to say they will likely have different takes about how to ultimately fill the gap in administering the statute.
sentences.zh: 我认为公平地说，他们对于最终如何填补管理法规中的空白可能会有不同的看法。

sentences.en: If you let every district court judge in the country decide for him or herself what a given regulation means, that's going to give rise to a kind of chaos,
sentences.zh: 如果你让全国的每一位地方法官自己决定某项法规意味着什么，那将会引发一种混乱，

sentences.en: to a kind of patchwork where people in Georgia are subject to different regulations than people in California.
sentences.zh: 一种拼凑的局面，佐治亚州的人受到的法规与加利福尼亚州的人不同。

sentences.en: And that's not a desirable result, she says.
sentences.zh: 她说，这不是一个理想的结果。

sentences.en: Thank you, counsel.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，律师。

sentences.en: The case is submitted.
sentences.zh: 案件已提交。

sentences.en: Okay, so Adam,
sentences.zh: 好的，亚当，

sentences.en: this is the part of any oral arguments episode where I need to ask you to kind of cut through the two sides of the argument and the liberal interrogations of the lawyers and the conservative interrogations of the lawyers.
sentences.zh: 这是任何口头辩论节目中我需要请你剖析辩论双方、律师受到的自由派质询以及律师受到的保守派质询的部分。

sentences.en: And tell us, with your predictive eye, how this case is likely to be decided.
sentences.zh: 并用你预测的眼光告诉我们，这个案件可能会如何判决。

sentences.en: Is the Chevron doctrine basically dead?
sentences.zh: 雪佛龙原则基本上死了吗？

sentences.en: Chevron is either dead or will survive in a kind of zombified, hollowed-out version where it doesn't do very much work or it does work in a very narrow band of cases.
sentences.zh: 雪佛龙原则要么已经死了，要么将以一种僵尸化的、被掏空的版本存活下来，它不会发挥太大作用，或者只在极少数案件中发挥作用。

sentences.en: But the short answer is that this is probably the case, this term, that overrules a major precedent like affirmative action in the last term, like abortion in the previous term.
sentences.zh: 但简短的回答是，这很可能是本届法院推翻重大先例的案件，就像上届法院的平权行动案，以及前一届的堕胎案一样。

sentences.en: The right side of the court usually has one big project, and I think this is the project for the current term.
sentences.zh: 法院的右翼通常有一个大项目，我认为这就是本届法院的项目。

sentences.en: That project being to overturn decades of deference to government agencies and clear a path for pretty sweeping deregulation in the United States.
sentences.zh: 这个项目就是推翻几十年来对政府机构的尊重，并为美国相当广泛的放松管制扫清道路。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the conservative legal movement has kind of social aspects to it, and abortion and Roe v.
sentences.zh: 所以保守派法律运动有某种社会层面，堕胎和罗诉韦德案长期以来一直是目标。

sentences.en: Wade was long a target.
sentences.zh: 但对于保守派法律运动中真正痛恨他们所称的行政国家的那部分人来说，雪佛龙原则就是等同的目标。

sentences.en: But Chevron is the equivalent for that part of the conservative legal movement that really hates what they call the administrative state.
sentences.zh: 推翻雪佛龙原则对他们来说将是一场巨大的胜利。

sentences.en: And taking down Chevron would be a huge victory for them.
sentences.zh: 推翻雪佛龙原则对他们来说将是一场巨大的胜利。

sentences.en: Adam, there's something distinct about this case if, as it turns out, it's the latest victory for the conservative movement.
sentences.zh: 亚当，如果事实证明这是保守派运动的最新胜利，那么这个案件就有其独特之处。

sentences.en: I mean, overturning Roe was about discouraging abortion, which the conservative movement abhors.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，推翻罗诉韦德案是为了阻止堕胎，这是保守派运动所厌恶的。

sentences.en: Ending affirmative action banned racial preferences, which conservatives view as unfair.
sentences.zh: 结束平权行动禁止了种族偏好，保守派认为这是不公平的。

sentences.en: This case, if conservatives win it, is going to end up giving a tremendous amount of power to the judiciary, as you've explained.
sentences.zh: 如果保守派赢得了这个案件，正如你所解释的那样，它最终将赋予司法机构巨大的权力。

sentences.en: And if you know anything about the American conservative movement, you know that for the longest time it has complained that unelected judges, especially, they say, liberal judges,
sentences.zh: 如果你对美国保守派运动有所了解，你就知道长期以来它一直抱怨未经选举的法官，特别是他们所说的自由派法官，

sentences.en: already have far too much power.
sentences.zh: 已经拥有了太多的权力。

sentences.en: So there's a kind of irony to the fact that this is a case that's going to put even more power into the hands of judges.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个将更多的权力交到法官手中的案件，这具有某种讽刺意味。

sentences.en: That's a good point, and it may be irony or it may be opportunism.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的观点，这可能是讽刺，也可能是机会主义。

sentences.en: The right was unhappy with liberal judges when there were a lot of liberal judges and when the court was reaching liberal results.
sentences.zh: 当有很多自由派法官且法院做出自由派结果时，右翼对自由派法官感到不满。

sentences.en: Now that the right controls the Supreme Court and is very powerful in the lower courts, it may take a different view.
sentences.zh: 现在右翼控制了最高法院，并在下级法院非常有权势，它可能会采取不同的观点。

sentences.en: It's also the case that the Supreme Court, in general, likes to be the decider.
sentences.zh: 最高法院通常也喜欢成为决策者。

sentences.en: It seems to decide every consequential social issue in the land, and getting rid of Chevron, among other things, increases judicial power, which the Supreme Court likes.
sentences.zh: 它似乎决定了国内每一个重要的社会问题，而废除雪佛龙原则等举措增加了司法权力，这是最高法院所喜欢的。

sentences.en: This Supreme Court likes.
sentences.zh: 这是最高法院所喜欢的。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, Adam, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好吧，亚当，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的事情。

sentences.en: On Thursday, for the fifth time in just a week, the United States attacked Houthi military sites inside Yemen to stop what it said was an imminent attack on ships in the Red Sea.
sentences.zh: 周四，美国在一周内第五次袭击了也门境内的胡塞武装军事地点，以阻止其所称的对红海船只的迫在眉睫的袭击。

sentences.en: Despite repeated U.S.
sentences.zh: 尽管美国一再

sentences.en: attacks, American officials say they have damaged or destroyed only about 20 to 30 percent of the Houthi's offensive capability,
sentences.zh: 袭击，美国官员表示他们只损坏或摧毁了胡塞武装约20%到30%的进攻能力，

sentences.en: suggesting that the group's attacks are likely to continue.
sentences.zh: 这表明该组织的袭击很可能会继续。

sentences.en: And, Mr. President, we have good news for America.
sentences.zh: 而且，总统先生，我们给美国带来了好消息。

sentences.en: There will not be a shutdown on Friday.
sentences.zh: 周五不会停摆。

sentences.en: On Thursday, Congress passed a last-minute, short-term funding bill that barely avoided a partial government shutdown.
sentences.zh: 周四，国会通过了一项最后一刻的短期拨款法案，勉强避免了政府部分停摆。

sentences.en: The bill, which would fund the government through March, was adopted over the strenuous opposition of far-right Republicans, who have demanded deep cuts to spending.
sentences.zh: 该法案将为政府提供资金至三月，是在极右翼共和党人的强烈反对下通过的，他们要求大幅削减开支。

sentences.en: And it marks the third time this fiscal year that Congress, unable to pass a long-term budget, has extended spending on a temporary basis.
sentences.zh: 这是本财年国会第三次在无法通过长期预算的情况下，临时延长支出。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Will Reed, Michael Simon-Johnson, and Astha Chaturvedi.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由威尔·里德、迈克尔·西蒙-约翰逊和阿斯塔·查图尔维迪制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by John Ketchum, contains original music by Dan Powell and Marion Lozano, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由约翰·凯彻姆编辑，包含丹·鲍威尔和马里昂·洛萨诺的原创音乐，并由克里斯·伍德进行工程制作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Lansford of Wonderland.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由仙境的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯福德创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you on Monday.
sentences.zh: 周一见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周在《Wirecutter秀》中，我们正在为假期接待做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人感到宾至如归的建议。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要完全黑暗才能睡觉的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是说他们是否会昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那是一件非常具体的事情。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在纽约时报应用程序或任何你喜欢收听的地方找到《Wirecutter秀》。
